items.finding: Tightened the newborn respiratory-rate wording to avoid presenting 30-60/min as a universal fixed range. AAP parent guidance supports rapid newborn breathing with rates up to about 40-60/min and flags >60/min as concerning when persistent.
Retained the age-related trend but removed an oversimplified single adult comparison. AAP states pediatric heart rate generally slows with age and provides age/awake/sleep ranges.
items.source_locator: AAP HealthyChildren, Normal Heart Rate Range for Children & Teens; reviewed 2026-08-14

items.finding: Kept central adiposity as an independent risk signal but removed wording that could imply waist circumference has identical predictive value across all populations. Item requires population-appropriate interpretation.
items.source_locator: AHA obesity/cardiometabolic risk guidance; currentness recheck required at final integration

items.finding: Changed the approximate threshold wording to the AHA interpretation that ABI <=0.90 supports lower-extremity PAD, avoiding vague 'below about 0.9' language.
items.source_locator: AHA Measurement and Interpretation of ABI, item 4; reviewed 2026-08-14

items.finding: Clarified that home INR testing supplements rather than replaces clinician-directed warfarin management. FDA specifically advises discussing expected results, testing frequency, and medication changes with the healthcare provider.
items.source_locator: FDA Tips for Patients and Caregivers Using INR Test Meters at Home; reviewed 2026-08-14

items.finding: The original stem implied therapeutic drug levels are generally drawn only after steady state. Rewritten to distinguish steady-state sampling from medications that require earlier peak/trough or loading-dose monitoring. Steady state remains a pharmacokinetic concept, not a universal timing rule for every drug level.
items.source_locator: OpenStax Pharmacology for Nurses 2.2, Half-Life / pharmacokinetics; reviewed 2026-08-14

items.finding: The 'expanded medication rights' framework is not sufficiently standardized for a strict single-best-answer item using the current generic ISMP citation. Item is held from FINAL_QA_PASS until a precise authoritative framework/source is selected or the question is rewritten around a directly sourced medication-safety behavior.

Reworded from absolute NPO language to pre-procedure fasting instructions tailored to anesthesia/sedation. The safety rationale remains reduction of regurgitation/aspiration risk, while fasting duration depends on intake and patient/procedure factors.
items.source_locator: ASA Made for This Moment, fasting/aspiration explanation; reviewed 2026-08-14

items.finding: Standardized axillary-crutch fitting to approximately two finger widths below the axilla, hand weight-bearing, and about 30 degrees elbow flexion instead of a loose 2-3 finger-width claim without the elbow criterion.

Removed the unsupported implication that generic 'sensory deprivation prevention' alone is a validated ICU-delirium intervention. Reframed around orientation, appropriate interaction, sleep-wake support, and avoiding unnecessary deprivation as components of supportive delirium-prevention care.
items.source_locator: AHRQ PSNet ICU delirium assessment/prevention discussion; reviewed 2026-08-14
